newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 21.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Monday:

- British prime minister Tony Blair could be forced to scrap the existing talks process if the Ulster Unionists carry out their threat to block his timetable for the start of all-party negotiations on the future of Northern Ireland.
- Provincial bus services face major disruption on Tuesday if talks at the Labour Relations Commission fail today.
- The Dunnes payments tribunal is likely to pursue its appeal against a decision of the Grand Court in the Cayman Islands preventing it from taking evidence there, sources have confirmed.
IRISH INDEPENDENT - Irish Steel, sold by the government for just one pound just 14 months ago, is now valued at more than 100 million by its new owners, Ispat International.

- Irish prime minister Bertie Ahern and British premier Tony Blair were last night striving to find a way of persuading the Ulster Unionist Party to join Sinn Fein in talks now that the IRA has renewed its ceasefire.
- A final effort to prevent a strike on all provincial bus services will be made in talks at the Labour Relations Commission today.
- Furious efforts to keep David Trimble's Ulster Unionist Party on board the peace process continued yesterday in Dublin and London following the second IRA cessation of violence.
- Darren Clarke was still shaking his head in disbelief last night at the shank off the tee at Troon's second hole which derailed his British Open challenge.
